WO25-00611.name: rate_card_variance_wo
WO25-00611.text: WO25-00611 is a road cave-in repair in ward B by Sahyadri Infra Works (fictional): excavation, pipeline repair and a PQC patch over 27.5 sqm, recorded at ₹410,330 against a rate-card expectation of ₹180,000. WO25-02486.name: duplicate_candidate_wo
WO25-02486.text: WO25-02486 raises a possible duplicate-billing question. It is a pump and debris removal job on RD0216 in ward L, recorded at ₹112,441 with no complaint linked, and it matches an earlier job on the same road, WO25-01255, in method and in area (2.8 sqm), three days earlier and with the same contractor. The costs differ by only about 0.55%. Neither the amount nor the method is unusual on its own; the pairing with no linked complaint is what makes it worth a site-evidence and linkage check. A duplicate candidate means please verify, not confirmed.

WO25-01723.name: surface_dlp_wo

BMC25-004589.name: unfixed_multilingual_complaint_near_hospital_corridor
BMC25-004589.text: A Hindi complaint, BMC25-004589, logged on the MyBMC app in mid-August 2025, says that flooding at Vikhroli (ward N) is stopping an ambulance from getting through. Its GPS pin lies about 3 metres from RD0251, an ambulance-entry road for an emergency hospital, and 24 people upvoted it, yet it is still open with no work order linked. Its category is marked unverified because the Hindi wording is generic, but the ambulance reference makes it a good first case for a ward officer to check.

RD0077.name: Eastern Express Highway
RD0077.text: RD0077, the Eastern Express Highway segment in ward F/N, tops the new-budget list with a risk score of 78. It has 6 open complaints nearby and 6 reopened repairs on record, and sits close to a flood hotspot. Most of its history points to waterlogging (2 open complaints and 4 reopened jobs), so the candidate treatment for engineering review is a dewatering pump deployment, estimated at ₹60,000 and affordable from the ward's remaining ₹1.09M. It appears in the top ten under all four weighting profiles we tested.

RD0180.name: Malad Subway
RD0180.text: RD0180, Malad Subway in ward P/N, ranks second (risk 74). Nine open complaints sit near it and 8 repairs have reopened within 30 days, and the road also touches a flood hotspot and a school. The dominant issue is potholes (6 open complaints plus 5 reopened jobs), so the candidate treatment for engineering review is a hot mix patch, about ₹16,120 and affordable within the ward's remaining ₹0.69M. It stays in the top ten under all four weighting profiles.

RD0173.name: Marve Road
RD0173.text: RD0173, Marve Road in ward P/N, ranks third (risk 67). Five open complaints and five reopened repairs point to potholes, and 6 accidents with road-surface causes are on record. The candidate treatment for engineering review is a hot mix patch, estimated at ₹17,420, which the ward's budget can cover. It is in the top ten under three of the four weighting profiles, so treat it as a strong but not unanimous pick.

RD0058.name: Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Road
RD0058.text: RD0058, Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Road in ward F/S, ranks fourth (risk 65). It combines 5 reopened repairs with two flood hotspots nearby and serves two emergency hospitals, which is why the score is high despite only one open complaint on record. The candidate treatment for engineering review is a dewatering pump deployment, about ₹60,000, affordable from the ward's ₹1.77M remaining.

RD0057.name: Bellasis Road
RD0057.text: RD0057, Bellasis Road in ward E, ranks fifth (risk 64), driven mainly by accident severity and four nearby schools. Three open complaints describe a cave-in, so the candidate treatment for engineering review is an excavation, pipeline repair and PQC patch, estimated at ₹180,000. Ward E is already ₹1.02M over its monsoon budget, so this is not affordable now; risk ranking is deliberately kept separate from affordability, which is why the road stays on the list.

_verification.method: Showcase narratives authored by Claude Sonnet 5.5 offline from verified pipeline numbers (every number is checked against computed values); remaining wards use deterministic summaries.
_verification.disclosure: Synthetic challenge dataset. Not official BMC data. Contractors, amounts, dates, coordinates and transactions are fictional. Real Mumbai geographic names are used only for challenge realism.
_verification.model_contribution_disclosure: Claude was used during development for multilingual interpretation and reviewed plain-language explanations grounded in deterministic PostGIS calculations. All monetary calculations, audit rules and rankings are deterministic and reproducible. The live demo works offline.
